name: Elsa Allen
life: “I still remember saving a neighbor's supper until the moon rose.” On Tuesday, near the bank steps, Elsa takes a few minutes to read the public notices, especially the ones written in a hurry.
voice: I was fasting when the first tray came out. The baker put my piece away without making a fuss.
appearance: On an ordinary day, look for a rust-colored canvas coat and a thin silver ring worn on a cord. Elsa has an aquiline nose and a square chin, with close-cropped dark curls. Elsa grins on one side while the eyes stay serious during a conversation.
personality: Elsa has a quick wit and an equally quick sense of shame. A joke is often Elsa's way of finding out whether a room is friendly enough for a serious question.
agenda: To collect the saved bun after the fast.
family: Sybil Rey is Elsa’s cousin. Elsa can always ask for five minutes alone. Sybil asks before bringing somebody along. It keeps a conversation between two people from unexpectedly turning into a family committee. Asked about *Two portions*, Sybil says, “The second portion costs less than my mileage for investigating it.”
connections: Carlo Gil. The seller sets a little spice packet aside for a customer fasting until night.

reactions.situation: A customer wants a bun saved until evening
reactions.response: Elsa writes the customer's name and collection time on the wrapped bun.

reactions.situation: Someone begins blaming the youngest worker for a missing item
reactions.response: Elsa asks everybody to retrace their own last ordinary actions before asking the young worker a question.

reactions.response: Elsa seeks out the person it hurt before telling anybody why it was supposed to be funny.
reactions.asWritten: If the joke lands badly, Elsa seeks out the person it hurt before telling anybody why it was supposed to be funny.
